CLEAN TRAFFIC DATA¶

In [7]:
traffic["datetime"] = (
    pd.to_datetime(traffic["calendar_date"], errors="coerce")
    + pd.to_timedelta(traffic["time_hh24"], unit="h")
)

traffic = traffic.dropna(subset=["datetime"]).copy()

# Use the supplied total traffic column where available
if "Unnamed: 13" in traffic.columns:
    traffic["traffic_volume"] = pd.to_numeric(
        traffic["Unnamed: 13"], errors="coerce"
    )
else:
    # Otherwise sum available traffic columns
    traffic_cols = [
        c for c in traffic.columns
        if c not in ["calendar_date", "time_hh24", "datetime"]
    ]
    traffic["traffic_volume"] = traffic[traffic_cols].apply(
        pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce"
    ).sum(axis=1)

traffic = traffic[["datetime", "traffic_volume"]]

traffic = (
    traffic.groupby("datetime", as_index=False)["traffic_volume"]
    .mean()
    .sort_values("datetime")
)

CLEAN AIR QUALITY DATA¶

In [8]:
def prepare_air_data(df):
    data = df.copy()

    data["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(data["Date"], errors="coerce")
    data["Time"] = pd.to_timedelta(data["Time"].astype(str), errors="coerce")

    data["datetime"] = data["Date"] + data["Time"]

    data["Value"] = pd.to_numeric(data["Value"], errors="coerce")

    data["Parameter"] = (
        data["Parameter"]
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
        .str.upper()
    )

    data = data.dropna(
        subset=["datetime", "Value", "Parameter"]
    )

    return data[["datetime", "Parameter", "Value"]]


aqi_clean = prepare_air_data(aqi)
pollution_clean = prepare_air_data(pollution)

air = pd.concat(
    [aqi_clean, pollution_clean],
    ignore_index=True
)

rename_map = {}

for col in air.columns:
    clean = col.replace("_", "").replace(".", "")

    if clean == "PM25":
        rename_map[col] = "PM2.5"

    elif clean == "PM10":
        rename_map[col] = "PM10"

    elif clean == "NO2":
        rename_map[col] = "NO2"

    elif clean == "O3":
        rename_map[col] = "O3"

    elif clean == "NOX":
        rename_map[col] = "NOx"

    elif clean == "NO":
        rename_map[col] = "NO"

    elif clean == "AQI":
        rename_map[col] = "AQI"

air = air.rename(columns=rename_map)

HANDLE MISSING VALUES¶

In [14]:
data = data.sort_values("datetime").copy()
data = data.drop_duplicates(subset=["datetime"], keep="last")
data = data.set_index("datetime").asfreq("h").reset_index()

# Do not interpolate or backward-fill target pollutants.
# Keep original missing target observations as missing.
desired_targets = ["PM2.5", "NO2", "O3"]

available_targets = [
    t for t in desired_targets if t in data.columns
]

print("Available targets:", available_targets)

# Fill only explanatory variables, using past information.
# Never use bfill or two-sided interpolation for model inputs.
target_columns = available_targets

numeric_columns = data.select_dtypes(
    include=np.number
).columns.tolist()

exogenous_columns = [
    c for c in numeric_columns
    if c not in target_columns
]

data[exogenous_columns] = data[exogenous_columns].ffill(limit=6)

print("Hourly observations:", len(data))
print("Target missingness:")
print(data[target_columns].isna().sum())

# 1. CONFIGURE OUTPUT DIRECTORY

OUTPUT_DIR = r"D:\Auckland_Air_Quality_MVP"

# Create the folder if it does not exist
os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)

print("Output folder:", os.path.abspath(OUTPUT_DIR))
print("Folder exists:", os.path.isdir(OUTPUT_DIR))

# 2. VALIDATE REQUIRED DATA

if "data" not in globals():
    raise NameError(
        "The DataFrame 'data' was not found. "
        "Run the cell that loads your dataset first."
    )

if "datetime" not in data.columns:
    raise KeyError(
        "The 'datetime' column is missing. "
        "Check your dataset's column names."
    )

# Convert datetime to the correct format
data["datetime"] = pd.to_datetime(
    data["datetime"],
    errors="coerce"
)

# Identify available target variables
# Uses your existing available_targets if it is defined
if "available_targets" in globals():
    available_targets = [
        col for col in available_targets
        if col in data.columns and col != "datetime"
    ]
else:
    # Automatically detect numeric measurement columns
    available_targets = [
        col for col in data.select_dtypes(include="number").columns
        if col != "datetime"
    ]

if not available_targets:
    raise ValueError(
        "No valid numeric target columns were found. "
        "Check your dataset and available_targets."
    )

print("\nTargets to plot:", available_targets)

# 3. CREATE TIME-SERIES PLOTS

successful_plots = []
skipped_targets = []

for target in available_targets:

    try:
        # Select and clean the required columns
        plot_data = data[["datetime", target]].copy()

        plot_data["datetime"] = pd.to_datetime(
            plot_data["datetime"],
            errors="coerce"
        )

        plot_data[target] = pd.to_numeric(
            plot_data[target],
            errors="coerce"
        )

        # Remove invalid timestamps and missing measurements
        plot_data = plot_data.dropna(
            subset=["datetime", target]
        )

        # Sort observations chronologically
        plot_data = plot_data.sort_values(
            "datetime"
        ).reset_index(drop=True)

        # Skip targets without usable observations
        if plot_data.empty:
            print(f"Skipping {target}: no valid observations.")
            skipped_targets.append(target)
            continue

        # Calculate rolling mean
        # A 24-row window represents 24 hours only when
        # observations are consistently hourly.
        plot_data["rolling_24h"] = (
            plot_data[target]
            .rolling(window=24, min_periods=1)
            .mean()
        )

        # Create figure
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(15, 6))

        ax.plot(
            plot_data["datetime"],
            plot_data[target],
            linewidth=0.7,
            alpha=0.45,
            label="Observed concentration"
        )

        ax.plot(
            plot_data["datetime"],
            plot_data["rolling_24h"],
            linewidth=2,
            label="24-observation rolling mean"
        )

        # Titles and axis labels
        ax.set_title(
            f"{target} Concentration: Time-Series Trend",
            fontsize=15,
            fontweight="bold"
        )

        ax.set_xlabel("Date")
        ax.set_ylabel(f"{target} concentration")
        ax.legend()
        ax.grid(alpha=0.2)

        fig.autofmt_xdate()
        fig.tight_layout()

        # Create a safe filename
        safe_target = re.sub(
            r'[<>:"/\\|?*]+',
            "_",
            str(target)
        ).strip(" .")

        filename = f"{safe_target}_enhanced_time_series.png"
        output_path = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, filename)

        # Save plot
        fig.savefig(
            output_path,
            dpi=300,
            bbox_inches="tight"
        )

        plt.show()
        plt.close(fig)

        # Confirm that the file was saved
        if os.path.isfile(output_path):
            successful_plots.append(output_path)
            print(f"Saved successfully: {output_path}")
        else:
            print(f"Warning: output file not found for {target}")

    except Exception as error:
        print(f"Error processing {target}: {error}")
        skipped_targets.append(target)

# 4. FINAL SUMMARY

print("\n" + "=" * 55)
print("TIME-SERIES VISUALISATION SUMMARY")
print("=" * 55)

print(f"Plots saved successfully: {len(successful_plots)}")
print(f"Targets skipped or failed: {len(skipped_targets)}")
print(f"Output directory: {os.path.abspath(OUTPUT_DIR)}")

if successful_plots:
    print("\nSaved files:")
    for path in successful_plots:
        print(path)

if skipped_targets:
    print("\nSkipped or failed targets:")
    for target in skipped_targets:
        print(target)

print("\nProcessing completed.")

In [22]:
for target in available_targets:

    heatmap_data = data.copy()

    heatmap_data["hour"] = (
        heatmap_data["datetime"].dt.hour
    )

    heatmap_data["day_name"] = (
        heatmap_data["datetime"]
        .dt.day_name()
    )

    day_order = [
        "Monday",
        "Tuesday",
        "Wednesday",
        "Thursday",
        "Friday",
        "Saturday",
        "Sunday"
    ]

    heatmap = heatmap_data.pivot_table(
        index="day_name",
        columns="hour",
        values=target,
        aggfunc="mean"
    )

    heatmap = heatmap.reindex(day_order)

    plt.figure(figsize=(15, 6))

    plt.imshow(
        heatmap,
        aspect="auto",
        interpolation="nearest"
    )

    plt.colorbar(
        label=f"Average {target}"
    )

    plt.xticks(
        range(24),
        range(24)
    )

    plt.yticks(
        range(7),
        day_order
    )

    plt.title(
        f"{target}: Pollution Intensity by Day and Hour",
        fontsize=15,
        fontweight="bold"
    )

    plt.xlabel("Hour of Day")
    plt.ylabel("Day of Week")

    plt.tight_layout()

    plt.savefig(
        os.path.join(
            OUTPUT_DIR,
            f"{target}_hour_day_heatmap.png"
        ),
        dpi=300,
        bbox_inches="tight"
    )

    plt.show()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# FEATURES: ONLY PAST TARGET AND PAST EXPLANATORY DATA
# ------------------------------------------------------------

def make_model_table(source, target):
    d = source.sort_values("datetime").copy()
    d = d.drop_duplicates("datetime", keep="last")
    d = d.reset_index(drop=True)

    # Use a regular hourly time grid.
    d = d.set_index("datetime").asfreq("h").reset_index()

    # Causal filling of explanatory variables only.
    other_targets = [
        t for t in ["PM2.5", "NO2", "O3"]
        if t in d.columns
    ]

    numeric_cols = d.select_dtypes(
        include=np.number
    ).columns.tolist()

    exog_cols = [
        c for c in numeric_cols
        if c not in other_targets
    ]

    d[exog_cols] = d[exog_cols].ffill(limit=6)

    # Calendar features are known in advance.
    d["hour"] = d["datetime"].dt.hour
    d["dayofweek"] = d["datetime"].dt.dayofweek
    d["month"] = d["datetime"].dt.month
    d["dayofyear"] = d["datetime"].dt.dayofyear

    d["hour_sin"] = np.sin(2 * np.pi * d["hour"] / 24)
    d["hour_cos"] = np.cos(2 * np.pi * d["hour"] / 24)
    d["doy_sin"] = np.sin(
        2 * np.pi * d["dayofyear"] / 365.25
    )
    d["doy_cos"] = np.cos(
        2 * np.pi * d["dayofyear"] / 365.25
    )

    feature_cols = [
        "hour", "dayofweek", "month", "dayofyear",
        "hour_sin", "hour_cos", "doy_sin", "doy_cos"
    ]

    # Historical target features: shift before rolling.
    for lag in [1, 2, 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, 72]:
        name = f"{target}_lag_{lag}"
        d[name] = d[target].shift(lag)
        feature_cols.append(name)

    for window in [3, 6, 12, 24]:
        mean_name = f"{target}_mean_{window}"
        std_name = f"{target}_std_{window}"

        d[mean_name] = (
            d[target].shift(1).rolling(window).mean()
        )
        d[std_name] = (
            d[target].shift(1).rolling(window).std()
        )

        feature_cols.extend([mean_name, std_name])

    # Other pollutants, weather and traffic are used with a
    # one-hour lag, not their same-hour values.
    for col in exog_cols:
        lag_name = f"{col}_lag1"
        d[lag_name] = d[col].shift(1)
        feature_cols.append(lag_name)

    # Explicit leakage guard.
    assert target not in feature_cols
    assert all(
        not name.startswith(target + "_lag0")
        for name in feature_cols
    )

    # Remove rows without an observed target or sufficient
    # historical information. Do not fill missing targets.
    d = d.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    d = d.dropna(subset=[target] + feature_cols).copy()

    return d, feature_cols


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# SIX MODELS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

def build_models():
    return {
        "Random Forest": RandomForestRegressor(
            n_estimators=200,
            max_depth=15,
            min_samples_leaf=2,
            random_state=42,
            n_jobs=-1
        ),

        "Gradient Boosting": GradientBoostingRegressor(
            n_estimators=150,
            learning_rate=0.05,
            max_depth=3,
            loss="huber",
            random_state=42
        ),

        "Neural Network": Pipeline([
            ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
            ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
            ("model", MLPRegressor(
                hidden_layer_sizes=(64, 32),
                activation="relu",
                max_iter=300,
                early_stopping=False,
                random_state=42
            ))
        ]),

        "Extra Trees": ExtraTreesRegressor(
            n_estimators=200,
            max_depth=15,
            min_samples_leaf=2,
            random_state=42,
            n_jobs=-1
        ),

        "Hist Gradient Boosting": HistGradientBoostingRegressor(
            max_iter=150,
            learning_rate=0.05,
            max_leaf_nodes=15,
            l2_regularization=1.0,
            random_state=42
        ),

        "Ridge Regression": Pipeline([
            ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
            ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
            ("model", Ridge(alpha=10.0))
        ])
    }


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# METRICS
# ------------------------------------------------------------

def calculate_metrics(y_true, y_pred):
    return {
        "MAE": mean_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred),
        "RMSE": np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred)),
        "R2": (
            r2_score(y_true, y_pred)
            if len(y_true) > 1 else np.nan
        )
    }


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# WALK-FORWARD VALIDATION + FINAL HOLDOUT
# ------------------------------------------------------------

all_test_results = []
all_cv_results = []
all_predictions = []
model_objects = {}

for target in TARGETS:

    print(f"\n========== {target} ==========")

    model_table, features = make_model_table(data, target)

    X = model_table[features]
    y = model_table[target]
    timestamps = model_table["datetime"]

    n = len(model_table)

    if n < 100:
        print(f"Insufficient modelling rows for {target}: {n}")
        continue

    # Final 15% is reserved as untouched test data.
    test_start = int(n * 0.85)

    X_dev, y_dev = X.iloc[:test_start], y.iloc[:test_start]
    X_test, y_test = X.iloc[test_start:], y.iloc[test_start:]

    time_test = timestamps.iloc[test_start:]

    # Walk-forward validation uses only development data.
    splitter = TimeSeriesSplit(n_splits=5)
    cv_scores = []
    models = build_models()

    for model_name, prototype in models.items():

        fold_number = 0

        for train_idx, val_idx in splitter.split(X_dev):

            fold_number += 1
            model = clone(prototype)

            X_train_fold = X_dev.iloc[train_idx]
            y_train_fold = y_dev.iloc[train_idx]
            X_val_fold = X_dev.iloc[val_idx]
            y_val_fold = y_dev.iloc[val_idx]

            model.fit(X_train_fold, y_train_fold)
            val_pred = model.predict(X_val_fold)

            metrics = calculate_metrics(y_val_fold, val_pred)

            cv_scores.append({
                "Pollutant": target,
                "Model": model_name,
                "Fold": fold_number,
                **metrics
            })

    cv_df = pd.DataFrame(cv_scores)
    all_cv_results.append(cv_df)

    # Select using mean walk-forward RMSE only.
    cv_summary = (
        cv_df.groupby(["Pollutant", "Model"], as_index=False)
        [["MAE", "RMSE", "R2"]]
        .mean()
        .rename(columns={
            "MAE": "CV_MAE",
            "RMSE": "CV_RMSE",
            "R2": "CV_R2"
        })
    )

    best_name = (
        cv_summary.sort_values("CV_RMSE")
        .iloc[0]["Model"]
    )

    print("Selected from walk-forward validation:", best_name)

    # Evaluate every model on the same final chronological test.
    fitted_models = {}

    for model_name, prototype in models.items():

        model = clone(prototype)
        model.fit(X_dev, y_dev)

        pred = model.predict(X_test)
        metrics = calculate_metrics(y_test, pred)

        all_test_results.append({
            "Pollutant": target,
            "Model": model_name,
            "Train_Observations": len(X_dev),
            "Test_Observations": len(X_test),
            "Test_Start": time_test.iloc[0],
            "Test_End": time_test.iloc[-1],
            **metrics
        })

        prediction_rows = pd.DataFrame({
            "datetime": time_test.values,
            "Pollutant": target,
            "Model": model_name,
            "Actual": y_test.values,
            "Predicted": pred
        })

        all_predictions.append(prediction_rows)
        fitted_models[model_name] = model

    # Refit selected model on all available eligible observations
    # for use in the future forecast only.
    final_model = clone(models[best_name])
    final_model.fit(X, y)

    model_objects[target] = {
        "model": final_model,
        "model_name": best_name,
        "features": features,
        "history": data.sort_values("datetime").copy(),
        "model_table": model_table
    }

    print(cv_summary.sort_values("CV_RMSE").to_string(index=False))

# Check whether SHAP is available
if SHAP_AVAILABLE:

    # Create output folder if it does not exist
    os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)

    print("Available model objects:")
    for target, obj in model_objects.items():
        print(f"\nTarget: {target}")
        if isinstance(obj, dict):
            print("Keys:", list(obj.keys()))
        else:
            print("Object type:", type(obj).__name__)

    for target, obj in model_objects.items():

        # Check dictionary structure
        if not isinstance(obj, dict):
            print(f"Skipping {target}: model entry is not a dictionary.")
            continue

        # Support common alternative key names
        model = obj.get(
            "best_model",
            obj.get("model", obj.get("best_estimator"))
        )

        features = obj.get(
            "features",
            obj.get("feature_columns", obj.get("X_columns"))
        )

        model_data = obj.get(
            "data",
            obj.get("model_data", obj.get("df"))
        )

        # Skip entries with missing information
        if model is None:
            print(
                f"Skipping {target}: no trained model found. "
                f"Available keys: {list(obj.keys())}"
            )
            continue

        if features is None or model_data is None:
            print(
                f"Skipping {target}: features or data are missing. "
                f"Available keys: {list(obj.keys())}"
            )
            continue

        # Validate feature columns
        features = list(features)
        missing_features = [
            col for col in features
            if col not in model_data.columns
        ]

        if missing_features:
            print(
                f"Skipping {target}: missing columns "
                f"{missing_features}"
            )
            continue

        # Select sample and remove invalid values
        X_sample = model_data[features].tail(500).copy()
        X_sample = X_sample.apply(
            lambda col: __import__("pandas").to_numeric(
                col, errors="coerce"
            )
        )
        X_sample = X_sample.dropna()

        if X_sample.empty:
            print(f"Skipping {target}: no valid feature rows.")
            continue

        # SHAP TreeExplainer for supported tree-based models
        if isinstance(
            model,
            (
                RandomForestRegressor,
                GradientBoostingRegressor
            )
        ):
            try:
                explainer = shap.TreeExplainer(model)
                shap_values = explainer.shap_values(X_sample)

                plt.figure()
                shap.summary_plot(
                    shap_values,
                    X_sample,
                    show=False
                )

                plt.tight_layout()

                safe_target = re.sub(
                    r'[<>:"/\\|?*]+', "_", str(target)
                )

                output_path = os.path.join(
                    OUTPUT_DIR,
                    f"{safe_target}_SHAP.png"
                )

                plt.savefig(
                    output_path,
                    dpi=300,
                    bbox_inches="tight"
                )
                plt.show()
                plt.close()

                print(f"SHAP plot saved: {output_path}")

            except Exception as e:
                print(f"SHAP failed for {target}: {e}")

        else:
            print(
                f"Skipping SHAP for {target}: "
                f"unsupported model type {type(model).__name__}. "
                "This section currently supports "
                "RandomForestRegressor and "
                "GradientBoostingRegressor."
            )

else:
    print(
        "\nSHAP is not installed. Install it with:\n"
        "!pip install shap"
    )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Validate inputs
# ------------------------------------------------------------

os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)

if "datetime" not in data.columns:
    raise ValueError("The dataset must contain a 'datetime' column.")

data = data.copy()
data["datetime"] = pd.to_datetime(data["datetime"], errors="coerce")
data = data.dropna(subset=["datetime"])
data = data.sort_values("datetime")
data = data.drop_duplicates(subset=["datetime"], keep="last")

if not model_objects:
    raise ValueError("model_objects is empty. Train your models first.")


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Forecasting function
# ------------------------------------------------------------

def forecast_next_24_hours(source, target, model, features):

    raw = source.copy()
    features = list(features)

    if target not in raw.columns:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Target '{target}' is not present in the dataset."
        )

    raw["datetime"] = pd.to_datetime(
        raw["datetime"], errors="coerce"
    )
    raw = raw.dropna(subset=["datetime"])
    raw = raw.sort_values("datetime")
    raw = raw.drop_duplicates("datetime", keep="last")

    # Convert all non-date columns to numeric where possible
    for col in raw.columns:
        if col != "datetime":
            raw[col] = pd.to_numeric(raw[col], errors="coerce")

    # Preserve the location of the latest actual target value
    raw = (
        raw.set_index("datetime")
        .asfreq("h")
        .reset_index()
    )

    actual_target = raw[target].notna()
    observed_positions = np.flatnonzero(actual_target.to_numpy())

    if len(observed_positions) < 73:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{target}: only {len(observed_positions)} actual "
            "observations are available. At least 73 are required."
        )

    origin_idx = observed_positions[-1]
    history = raw.iloc[:origin_idx + 1].copy().reset_index(drop=True)

    # Forward-fill using past values only.
    # This handles short or long gaps without using future observations.
    numeric_cols = history.select_dtypes(
        include=np.number
    ).columns.tolist()

    history[numeric_cols] = history[numeric_cols].ffill()

    forecasts = []

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Forecast the next 24 hours recursively
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    for step in range(24):

        next_time = (
            history["datetime"].iloc[-1]
            + pd.Timedelta(hours=1)
        )

        hour = next_time.hour
        dayofweek = next_time.dayofweek
        month = next_time.month
        dayofyear = next_time.dayofyear

        time_features = {
            "hour": hour,
            "dayofweek": dayofweek,
            "month": month,
            "dayofyear": dayofyear,
            "hour_sin": np.sin(2 * np.pi * hour / 24),
            "hour_cos": np.cos(2 * np.pi * hour / 24),
            "doy_sin": np.sin(2 * np.pi * dayofyear / 365.25),
            "doy_cos": np.cos(2 * np.pi * dayofyear / 365.25),
        }

        row = {}

        # Generate exactly the feature names expected by the model
        for feature in features:

            # Time features
            if feature in time_features:
                row[feature] = time_features[feature]
                continue

            # Rolling features: e.g. PM2.5_mean_6, PM2.5_std_24
            rolling_match = re.fullmatch(
                r"(.+)_(mean|std)_(\d+)", feature
            )

            if rolling_match:
                base_col = rolling_match.group(1)
                statistic = rolling_match.group(2)
                window = int(rolling_match.group(3))

                if base_col not in history.columns:
                    row[feature] = np.nan
                    continue

                series = history[base_col].ffill().dropna()
                values = series.tail(window)

                if len(values) < window:
                    row[feature] = np.nan
                elif statistic == "mean":
                    row[feature] = float(values.mean())
                else:
                    row[feature] = float(values.std(ddof=1))

                continue

            # Lag features: e.g. AQI_lag1, PM2.5_lag_1
            lag_match = re.fullmatch(
                r"(.+)_lag_?(\d+)", feature
            )

            if lag_match:
                base_col = lag_match.group(1)
                lag = int(lag_match.group(2))

                if base_col not in history.columns:
                    row[feature] = np.nan
                    continue

                series = history[base_col].ffill()

                if len(series) >= lag:
                    value = series.iloc[-lag]
                    row[feature] = (
                        float(value) if pd.notna(value) else np.nan
                    )
                else:
                    row[feature] = np.nan

                continue

            # Direct features, if any, use the latest known value
            if feature in history.columns:
                value = history[feature].iloc[-1]
                row[feature] = (
                    float(value) if pd.notna(value) else np.nan
                )
            else:
                row[feature] = np.nan

        # Keep exactly the training feature order
        X_future = pd.DataFrame(
            [[row.get(col, np.nan) for col in features]],
            columns=features
        )

        X_future = X_future.replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        )

        if X_future.isna().any().any():
            missing = X_future.columns[
                X_future.isna().any()
            ].tolist()

            raise ValueError(
                f"{target}: these training features could not be "
                f"constructed: {missing}. Check whether these columns "
                "exist in the source data and whether the same feature "
                "engineering was used during model training."
            )

        prediction = float(model.predict(X_future)[0])

        forecasts.append({
            "datetime": next_time,
            "Pollutant": target,
            "Forecast": prediction,
            "Forecast_Step": step + 1,
            "Model": model_objects[target].get(
                "model_name", type(model).__name__
            ),
            "Forecast_Assumption":
                "Recursive target forecast; other variables held "
                "at their latest available values"
        })

        # Append the forecast hour.
        # Other variables retain their last known values.
        new_row = history.iloc[-1].copy()
        new_row["datetime"] = next_time
        new_row[target] = prediction

        history = pd.concat(
            [history, new_row.to_frame().T],
            ignore_index=True
        )

        history["datetime"] = pd.to_datetime(history["datetime"])

        for col in history.columns:
            if col != "datetime":
                history[col] = pd.to_numeric(
                    history[col], errors="coerce"
                )

        # Fill any remaining gaps using past values only
        numeric_cols = history.select_dtypes(
            include=np.number
        ).columns.tolist()

        history[numeric_cols] = history[numeric_cols].ffill()

    return pd.DataFrame(forecasts)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Generate all pollutant forecasts
# ------------------------------------------------------------

forecast_frames = []

for target, obj in model_objects.items():

    if not isinstance(obj, dict):
        print(f"Skipping {target}: model entry is not a dictionary.")
        continue

    if "model" not in obj or "features" not in obj:
        print(
            f"Skipping {target}: 'model' or 'features' is missing. "
            f"Available keys: {list(obj.keys())}"
        )
        continue

    print(f"Forecasting {target}...")

    forecast_part = forecast_next_24_hours(
        data,
        target,
        obj["model"],
        obj["features"]
    )

    forecast_frames.append(forecast_part)

if not forecast_frames:
    raise ValueError(
        "No forecasts were generated. Check model_objects."
    )

forecast_long = pd.concat(
    forecast_frames, ignore_index=True
)

forecast_24 = (
    forecast_long.pivot(
        index="datetime",
        columns="Pollutant",
        values="Forecast"
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Export forecast results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

24-HOUR WALK-FORWARD BACKTEST¶

In [36]:
backtest_rows = []

for target, obj in model_objects.items():

    table = obj["model_table"].sort_values("datetime").copy()
    features = obj["features"]

    # Use the selected model family.
    prototype = build_models()[obj["model_name"]]

    # Candidate origins are spaced seven days apart to reduce
    # overlap between forecast windows.
    first_origin = max(72, int(len(table) * 0.70))
    last_origin = len(table) - 24

    origins = list(range(first_origin, last_origin, 168))

    for origin in origins:

        train = table.iloc[:origin].copy()
        future = table.iloc[origin:origin + 24].copy()

        if len(future) != 24:
            continue

        X_train = train[features]
        y_train = train[target]

        model = clone(prototype)
        model.fit(X_train, y_train)

        # Forecast using recursive target lags and only
        # information available at the forecast origin.
        origin_time = table.iloc[origin - 1]["datetime"]

        raw_until_origin = data[
            data["datetime"] <= origin_time
        ].copy()

        if raw_until_origin[target].notna().sum() < 73:
            continue

        recursive = forecast_next_24_hours(
            raw_until_origin,
            target,
            model,
            features
        )

        # Match each predicted timestamp with the observed value.
        actual = future[
            ["datetime", target]
        ].rename(columns={target: "Actual"})

        matched = actual.merge(
            recursive[["datetime", "Forecast"]],
            on="datetime",
            how="inner"
        ).dropna()

        if len(matched) != 24:
            # Missing actual observations mean this origin is
            # not a complete 24-hour evaluation window.
            continue

        metrics = calculate_metrics(
            matched["Actual"],
            matched["Forecast"]
        )

        backtest_rows.append({
            "Pollutant": target,
            "Model": obj["model_name"],
            "Origin": origin_time,
            "Horizon_Hours": 24,
            "Evaluated_Hours": len(matched),
            **metrics
        })

backtest_24h = pd.DataFrame(backtest_rows)

backtest_24h.to_csv(
    os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "24h_walk_forward_backtest.csv"),
    index=False
)

if not backtest_24h.empty:
    print("\n24-HOUR WALK-FORWARD BACKTEST")
    print(backtest_24h.to_string(index=False))

    backtest_summary = (
        backtest_24h.groupby(
            ["Pollutant", "Model"], as_index=False
        )
        [["MAE", "RMSE", "R2"]]
        .mean()
    )

    backtest_summary.to_csv(
        os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "24h_backtest_summary.csv"),
        index=False
    )
else:
    print(
        "No complete 24-hour windows could be evaluated. "
        "Check target coverage and historical feature availability."
    )

    ax.axhline(

    # Mark maximum forecast

    ax.scatter(

AIR QUALITY SUMMARY FOR DECISION MAKING¶

In [43]:
summary = []

for target in available_targets:

    summary.append({
        "Pollutant": target,
        "Mean": data[target].mean(),
        "Minimum": data[target].min(),
        "Maximum": data[target].max(),
        "Std_Dev": data[target].std(),
        "Latest_Value": data[target].iloc[-1],
        "Forecast_24h_Mean":
            forecast_24[target].mean(),
        "Forecast_24h_Max":
            forecast_24[target].max()
    })

summary_df = pd.DataFrame(summary)

print("\n==============================")
print("AIR QUALITY DECISION SUMMARY")
print("==============================")

print(summary_df)

summary_df.to_csv(
    os.path.join(
        OUTPUT_DIR,
        "air_quality_summary.csv"
    ),
    index=False
)

# 1. Historical observations for date and pollutant filtering
historical_export = data.copy()
historical_export["Date"] = historical_export["datetime"].dt.date
historical_export["Year"] = historical_export["datetime"].dt.year
historical_export["Month"] = historical_export["datetime"].dt.month

historical_export.to_csv(
    os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "powerbi_historical_data.csv"),
    index=False
)

# 2. Model performance: all six models, both pollutants
model_results.to_csv(
    os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "powerbi_model_metrics.csv"),
    index=False
)

# 3. Actual versus predicted values for interactive charts
prediction_results.to_csv(
    os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "powerbi_test_predictions.csv"),
    index=False
)

# 4. Walk-forward validation fold results
walk_forward_results.to_csv(
    os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "powerbi_walk_forward.csv"),
    index=False
)

# 5. Long-format 24-hour forecast table
forecast_long.to_csv(
    os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "powerbi_forecast.csv"),
    index=False
)

# 6. Forecast summary
forecast_summary.to_csv(
    os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "powerbi_forecast_summary.csv"),
    index=False
)

# 7. Optional 24-hour backtest results
if "backtest_24h" in globals():
    backtest_24h.to_csv(
        os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, "powerbi_24h_backtest.csv"),
        index=False
    )

print("Power BI data exports completed:")
for filename in [
    "powerbi_historical_data.csv",
    "powerbi_model_metrics.csv",
    "powerbi_test_predictions.csv",
    "powerbi_walk_forward.csv",
    "powerbi_forecast.csv",
    "powerbi_forecast_summary.csv"
]:
    print(os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, filename))
